author: bnferguson
body:
## Background

  Claude Code sessions burn tokens on CLI commands (grep, find, cat, etc.) that
   have lighter-weight equivalents via [RTK](https://www.rtk-ai.app/). RTK
  provides a `rewrite` subcommand that can transparently swap these out, but
  it needs a PreToolUse hook to intercept commands before they run.

  Additionally, `rtk` and `claude-code` themselves weren't tracked in the
  Brewfile, meaning a fresh machine setup wouldn't install them.

  ## Solution

  - **RTK PreToolUse hook** (`claude/config/hooks/rtk-rewrite.sh`):
  Intercepts Bash tool calls, delegates to `rtk rewrite` to swap commands for
   token-saving equivalents. Includes version guards (requires rtk >= 0.23.0),
  dependency checks (jq), and respects Claude Code's permission model (deny
  rules pass through, ask rules prompt the user).
  - **Integrity checksum** (`.rtk-hook.sha256`): SHA256 of the hook script so
   it can be verified after cloning.
  - **CLAUDE.md**: Added `@RTK.md` reference for RTK-specific instructions.
  - **Brewfile**: Added `rtk` (formula) and `claude-code` (cask).

  ## Reviewer Notes

  - The hook is a thin shell wrapper — all rewrite logic lives in `rtk
  rewrite` (Rust binary), so this shouldn't need frequent updates.
  - The exit code protocol (0/1/2/3) is documented in the script header and
  maps cleanly to Claude Code's permission model.

  ## Testing Plan

  - [x] `brew bundle check` passes with the updated Brewfile
  - [ ] Start a Claude Code session in a project with the hook configured —
  verify commands like `grep` get rewritten to rtk equivalents
  - [ ] Verify the hook exits cleanly when rtk is not installed (warning only,
  no failure)
  - [x] Verify the sha256 matches: `cd claude/config/hooks && sha256sum -c
  .rtk-hook.sha256`

author: fishy49
body:
Adds branching outcomes to dice rolls defined in world JSON, ensuring players are never deadlocked. Each roll directive requires both an `on_success` and `on_failure` block, each with a message and a directive action (set flag, unlock dialogue, unlock exit). Invalid world data (missing a branch) is rejected at load time.

Spec: specs/pr-36-dice_roll_directives.md

## Build Progress

- [x] Ingest (started 11:05 UTC · finished 11:06 UTC)
- [x] Plan (started 11:06 UTC · finished 13:25 UTC)
- [x] Implement (started 13:25 UTC)

## Summary

Add dice roll directives to the classic game engine so that items can trigger skill checks with branching outcomes (success/failure), each executing directives like setting flags, unlocking dialogue, or unlocking exits.

### Changes
- **RollHandler** — new handler that resolves pending dice rolls against a DC, executes the winning branch's directives, and returns the outcome message; also returns the `DiceRoll` result object so the job layer can create a dice event message
- **BaseHandler** — added `pending_roll?` and `execute_roll_directives` protected helpers for processing `sets_flag`, `unlocks_dialogue`, and `unlocks_exit` directives
- **CommandParser** — added `roll` verb to the verb list and no-argument parsing branch
- **Engine** — added priority intercept for `pending_roll` state (routes all input to RollHandler), added `:roll` to handler routing, added `validate_world_data` class method for dice roll branch validation and `consume_on` value validation
- **ItemHandler** — added `handle_dice_roll_trigger` to set `pending_roll` state when using an item with a `dice_roll` definition; added re-trigger guard that short-circuits with `completed_message` when the success flag is already set
- **ContainerHandler** — added `unlock_flag` support: if a container has an `"unlock_flag"` key and that flag is set, it opens without requiring the key item
- **ClassicCommandJob** — creates an `event_type: "roll"` event message (with dice breakdown) before the text response when a roll resolves, so the ASCII dice partials render
- **Game model** — calls `Engine.validate_world_data` at setup time to reject items with incomplete dice roll branches

### `consume_on` directive

Items with a `dice_roll` block can specify when the item is consumed:

```json
"dice_roll": {
  "dc": 12,
  "consume_on": "failure",
  "completed_message": "The chest lock is already open.",
  ...
}
```

| Value | Behaviour |
|-------|-----------|
| `"failure"` | Item removed from inventory on failed roll (e.g. lockpick snaps) |
| `"success"` | Item consumed on successful roll |
| `"any"` | Always consumed after rolling |
| *(omitted)* | Item stays in inventory |

The `completed_message` field (optional, default `"Nothing happens."`) is shown when a player tries to re-use an item whose `on_success.sets_flag` is already set.

### Bug fixes (post-implementation QA)

**Successful lockpick roll didn't unlock the chest** — `on_success` correctly set `tavern_lockpick_success` in `global_flags`, but `ContainerHandler` only checked `unlock_item` (key in inventory) and never consulted flags. Fixed by adding `unlock_flag` support to `ContainerHandler` and adding `"unlock_flag": "tavern_lockpick_success"` to the QA world chest.

**No dice ASCII after a classic game ROLL** — the ASCII dice partials only rendered for `event_type: "roll"` messages, which were only created by the AI game's `/roll` command. The classic ROLL command returned a plain host message. Fixed by having `ClassicCommandJob` create a roll event message when the engine result includes a `dice_roll` object.

### Dev tooling fix
The **Reset Game** button in the debug view now uses `load` instead of `require` (picks up changes to `qa_world_data.rb` without a server restart) and recreates the QA world if it was deleted rather than silently returning.

### Test results
- Unit: 110 runs, 309 assertions, 0 failures
- System: 8 dice roll tests, 36 total QA world tests (all passing)

body:
### Motivation
- Clipboard ownership was lost because the SDL video subsystem was initialized and shut down inside `copy_text_to_clipboard()`, making pastes on X11 unreliable.
- Global hotkey toggles felt flaky because toggle checks only ran in the outer loop and the inner audio capture loop and VAD wait paths were not responsive to requests.
- Resuming a hotkey session left stale audio/context (`pcmf32_old`, `prompt_tokens`, etc.) which corrupted subsequent transcriptions.
- Mixed use of X11 from the hotkey thread and SDL in the main thread risked undefined behavior without `XInitThreads()`.

### Description
- Rewrote `copy_text_to_clipboard()` to require the SDL video subsystem be initialized and to call `SDL_PumpEvents()` after `SDL_SetClipboardText()` so the app does not immediately drop clipboard ownership.
- Call `XInitThreads()` at program start when X11 hotkey support is enabled and initialize the SDL video subsystem once (if hotkey/clipboard is used) instead of initializing and quitting it per copy.
- Introduced `reset_stream_state`, `pause_stream`, `resume_stream`, and `handle_hotkey_toggle` helpers and used them to centralize pause/resume logic and ensure a consistent state transition.
- On pause/resume, fully reset streaming state by clearing `pcmf32`, `pcmf32_old`, `pcmf32_new`, `prompt_tokens`, resetting `n_iter` and `t_last`, and clearing the audio buffer to prevent stale audio/context from leaking into resumed sessions.
- Made hotkey handling responsive by invoking `handle_hotkey_toggle()` in the outer loop, inside the non-VAD inner capture loop, and in VAD wait/capture paths, and added guards to skip inference on partial chunks after a toggle.
- Moved `--save-audio` writes to occur immediately after fresh audio capture in both non-VAD and VAD paths to avoid repeatedly writing stale buffers.

### Testing
- Attempted configuration with `cmake -S . -B build -DWHISPER_SDL2=ON -DWHISPER_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON`, which failed because the environment lacks the SDL2 development package (`SDL2Config.cmake` / `sdl2-config.cmake` not found), so a full build/test could not be completed in this container.
- Performed automated code searches to verify modified symbols and insertion points (no runtime tests executed due to missing SDL2).

author: denis-st-woof-software
body:
## Summary

Fix `sources-update` sync to preserve remote `asset` and `source` ids during insert and prevent PostgreSQL sequence drift after explicit-id inserts.

## Problem

`sources-update` relies on remote ids being stable and matchable across sync runs.

Before this change:
- new `asset` and `source` rows were inserted through TypeORM generated PK flow
- explicit remote ids were not reliably persisted on insert
- PostgreSQL sequences could lag behind real table data
- later inserts could fail with duplicate primary key errors

## What changed

- added explicit SQL insert methods for new assets and sources
  - `insertAssetsWithIds(...)`
  - `insertSourcesWithIds(...)`
- kept remote ids as authoritative during sync
- added sequence alignment after explicit-id inserts
  - `alignAssetIdSequence(...)`
  - `alignSourceIdSequence(...)`
- optimized asset insert flow with `RETURNING`
- limited sequence realignment to runs that actually insert new rows
- added inline comments explaining why these methods exist

## Why this approach

TypeORM `save()` with generated primary keys is not a safe fit for this sync flow, because the sync logic depends on local ids staying equal to remote ids.

Using explicit SQL inserts makes that contract deterministic, and sequence realignment prevents future PK collisions.

## Result

- `sources-update` preserves remote ids correctly
- repeated sync runs can match records by id reliably
- PostgreSQL sequences stay aligned with inserted data
- duplicate PK failures caused by sequence drift are avoided

The last commit is actually a generic zephyr fix that I'll push upstream. It's not strictly required, except that buffer memory needs to be increased if the change is not taken along.

Content:

- Hardcoded support for DNS service subtypes. A service like "_universal._sub._ipp._tcp" can be registered next to the "_ipp._tcp" service. Usually, the services would point to the same text records.
- The parsing of servicename/app-proto/transport-pro in zephyr is quite hardcoded, so an explicit comparison for this new subtype service is added and hardcoded (function dns_sd_query_extract).
- If a subtype service is requested (PTR request), the device must answer with the main service. See Changes in function add_ptr_record.
- If a subtype service is requested (PTR request), the device must also answer with a PTR for the main service (changes in dns_sd_handle_ptr_query).

author: rayston92
body:
## Summary
- Add macOS System Tray icon with a 360x480 floating panel showing wallet balance, watchlist tickers, and pending transactions
- New Preferences setting "Menu Bar" (macOS only, default on) to toggle the tray at runtime
- Native OS notifications on tx confirm/fail, click-to-navigate for panel items

## Intent & Context
macOS users want quick access to wallet overview without unfocusing their current work. The main OneKey window is heavyweight and hides into the dock; a menu-bar panel gives an always-available read-only view of portfolio state with one click, mirroring common macOS wallet patterns (Rainbow, Frame, etc.).

## Design Decisions
- **Separate BrowserWindow (not a native menu)** — lets us reuse the full React/Tamagui stack and existing components. The tray window loads the same webpack bundle with \`?render=tray\`, branching in \`App.tsx\` to mount a minimal \`TrayPanelApp\`.
- **IPC polling architecture** — main process owns the tray lifecycle and polls the main window renderer every 30s via \`TRAY_DATA_REQUEST\`. The renderer gathers data from Jotai atoms + backgroundApiProxy and responds with \`TRAY_DATA_RESPONSE\`. Polling only runs while the panel is visible, and there is a guard against overlapping requests.
- **IPC (not DOM events) for data-request forwarding** — switching the main window to \`contextIsolation: true\` broke the old \`globalThis.dispatchEvent\` pattern (preload and renderer worlds are isolated). Renderer now subscribes directly via \`desktopApi.addIpcEventListener(TRAY_IPC.DATA_REQUEST, …)\`.
- **Error fallback with \`isError\` flag** — on data-gathering failure the renderer sends empty \`pendingTxs\`, but tags the payload with \`isError: true\` so \`trayIpc.ts\` skips \`diffAndNotify\`. Prevents false \"Transaction Confirmed\" notifications on transient failures.
- **Runtime toggle via dedicated IPC** — \`TRAY_TOGGLE(boolean)\` channel. Main process inits the tray unconditionally at startup (matching \`settingsAtomInitialValue\`); renderer sends \`toggleTray(false)\` at mount if the user has disabled it. Default is on so upgrading users get the feature automatically — matched in both the atom initial value, the getter fallback (\`?? true\`), and the Switch UI default.
- **Platform guards** — all tray code is gated by \`isMac\` in main and \`platformEnv.isDesktopMac\` in renderer. Zero impact on Windows/Linux/mobile/web/extension.
- **Tray init after recovery-mode check** — \`initTrayManager\` runs only when the app passes the boot-fail-count recovery gate, so a recovery session doesn't show a non-functional tray icon.

## Changes Detail
**Main process** (\`apps/desktop/app/tray/\`)
- \`TrayManager.ts\` — lifecycle (create/destroy), polling guard, start/stop polling on panel visibility
- \`trayWindow.ts\` — frameless transparent 360x480 window, position relative to tray icon, hide on blur/Escape
- \`trayIpc.ts\` — data response handler, action allowlist, lock-state sync, skip diff on \`isError\`
- \`trayNotification.ts\` — diff pending tx list, fire native OS notifications on confirm/fail

**Main process integration** (\`apps/desktop/app/\`)
- \`app.ts\` — \`initTrayManager\` after recovery-mode check, \`TRAY_TOGGLE\` listener, \`destroyTrayManager\` on \`before-quit\`
- \`config.ts\` — 5 new IPC channel keys (\`TRAY_DATA_REQUEST/RESPONSE/UPDATE/ACTION/TOGGLE\`)
- \`preload.ts\` — add \`sendTrayData\`/\`toggleTray\`, add TRAY channels to listener allowlist, forward \`TRAY_DATA_REQUEST\` via IPC listener (not DOM event)
- Delete \`preloadTray.ts\` — superseded by full preload since the tray bundle needs the complete \`desktopApi\` surface to initialize

**Renderer** (\`packages/kit/src/\`)
- \`views/Tray/TrayPanel.tsx\` + 4 sub-components (\`PortfolioOverview\`, \`WatchlistTickers\`, \`PendingTransactions\`, \`TrayEmptyState\`) — read-only panel UI with loading / locked / noWallet / noContent / offline states
- \`hooks/useTrayDataProvider.desktop.ts\` — gathers wallet/balance/watchlist/pending-txs from backgroundApiProxy, subscribes to lock/account/history events for reactive updates, syncs tray-enabled state on mount
- \`views/Setting/pages/Tab/CustomElement.tsx\` + \`config.tsx\` — \`MenuBarTrayListItem\` toggle in Preferences (macOS only)
- \`provider/Bootstrap.tsx\` — mount data provider under \`AccountSelectorProviderMirror\`

**Background** (\`packages/kit-bg/src/\`)
- \`services/ServiceSetting.ts\` — \`getEnableMenuBarTray\` / \`setEnableMenuBarTray\` with \`?? true\` fallback
- \`states/jotai/atoms/settings.ts\` — new persist field \`enableMenuBarTray\` with default \`true\`

**Entry** (\`apps/desktop/App.tsx\`) — branch to \`TrayPanelApp\` when \`?render=tray\`, subscribe to system \`prefers-color-scheme\` for live theme updates

**i18n** — \`settings_menu_bar_tray\` and \`settings_menu_bar_tray_desc\` registered on Lokalise, all locales pulled

**Shared types** (\`packages/shared/src/types/desktop/tray.ts\`) — \`ITrayData\`, \`ITrayWatchlistItem\`, \`IPendingTx\`, \`TRAY_IPC\` constants

## Risk Assessment
- **Risk Level**: Medium
- **Affected Platforms**: Desktop (macOS only)
- **Risk Areas**:
  - New IPC surface: mitigated by action-type allowlist in \`trayIpc.ts\` and channel whitelist in \`preload.ts\`
  - Main window preload changes: TRAY channels added to event listener whitelist; \`sendTrayData\`/\`toggleTray\` exposed. \`sendTrayAction\` intentionally NOT exposed in main preload to avoid a self-forwarding IPC loop
  - Tray window uses full preload (not a minimal one) — required because the tray window loads the complete app bundle at init, and modules like \`useVisibilityChange\`, \`NotificationProvider\`, and \`DesktopWebView\` access \`desktopApi\` methods at module-evaluation time. Trade-off is documented; the tray panel only renders first-party market data
  - Lock state flows from renderer to main via \`isLocked: true\` in \`sendTrayData\` — \`requestDataFromMainWindow\` early-returns when \`isLocked\`
  - Migration path: existing users upgrading from versions without \`enableMenuBarTray\` default to ON via \`?? true\` in the getter and in the Switch UI

## Test plan
- [ ] macOS: tray icon appears on startup; click opens 360x480 panel
- [ ] Panel shows correct wallet name / emoji, total balance, 24h change
- [ ] Watchlist shows spot + perps tokens with icons and prices
- [ ] Pending tx list updates within seconds of sending a tx
- [ ] Clicking a spot ticker navigates main window to market detail
- [ ] Clicking a perps ticker switches to Perp tab with correct active asset
- [ ] Clicking portfolio header navigates to home tab
- [ ] Clicking a pending tx navigates to transaction detail
- [ ] OS notification fires on tx confirm/fail; clicking opens main window at tx
- [ ] Panel hides on blur / Escape
- [ ] Switching wallet in main app refreshes tray panel
- [ ] Locking app: panel shows \"App is Locked\", polling stops
- [ ] Settings > Preferences > Menu Bar toggle: tray icon creates / destroys at runtime
- [ ] Fresh install: tray is ON by default
- [ ] Upgrade from prior version: tray is ON by default (no persisted \`enableMenuBarTray\`)
- [ ] Transient data-fetch errors do NOT trigger false \"Transaction Confirmed\" notifications for tracked pending txs
- [ ] Theme: dark / light system theme changes update the panel live
- [ ] Recovery mode (3x boot fail): tray is NOT created
- [ ] Windows / Linux: no tray icon, no errors, zero impact

author: sj-i
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a hybrid phpspy mode that combines reli's ZTS-aware EG address resolution with phpspy's fast C-based tracing backend. Users can now use phpspy for tracing while reli handles the complex task of resolving executor globals (EG) addresses, including for ZTS (thread-safe) PHP builds where phpspy alone cannot operate.

## Key Changes

### New Commands
- **`phpspy:install`** - Install or verify phpspy binary availability with automatic installation from source
- **`phpspy:trace`** - Single-process tracing using phpspy as the backend (reli resolves EG, phpspy does tracing)
- **`phpspy:daemon`** - Multi-process daemon mode using phpspy backend with concurrent tracing support

### Core Components
- **`PhpSpyProcess`** - Manages phpspy subprocess lifecycle (start, stop, I/O handling)
  - Builds command-line arguments from settings
  - Handles non-blocking I/O for stdout/stderr
  - Provides process status monitoring
  
- **`PhpSpyFinder`** - Locates phpspy binary with fallback chain:
  1. Explicit `--phpspy-path` option
  2. `PHPSPY_PATH` environment variable
  3. `~/.reli/bin/phpspy` (default install location)
  4. System `which phpspy`

- **`PhpSpyProcessPool`** - Manages multiple concurrent phpspy processes for daemon mode
  - Attach/detach processes by PID
  - Passthrough output from all running processes
  - Track active process PIDs

### Settings & Configuration
- **`PhpSpySettings`** - Configuration object with defaults:
  - `sleep_ns`: 10101010 (sampling interval)
  - `buffer_size`: 4096
  - `rate_hz`: 99
  - Support for extra custom arguments

- **`PhpSpySettingsFromConsoleInput`** - Console option parsing for phpspy settings

### Binary Analysis Improvements
- **`BinaryFingerprintCreator`** - New class to create fingerprints including actual ELF header content
  - Reads ELF header from process memory to distinguish NTS vs ZTS builds
  - Falls back to metadata-based fingerprinting on read failure
  - Enables accurate binary caching even for identical metadata

- **`BinaryFingerprint`** - Enhanced with ELF header support
  - New `fromProcessModuleMemoryMapAndElfHeader()` method
  - Distinguishes between NTS and ZTS builds of same binary

### Testing
- Comprehensive test coverage for all new components
- Tests for process management, settings parsing, binary fingerprinting
- Process pool lifecycle tests

## Implementation Details

The hybrid mode workflow:
1. User specifies target process (PID or command)
2. Reli resolves the EG (executor globals) address, including ZTS support via TSRM
3. Reli launches phpspy with the resolved EG address and other parameters
4. phpspy performs fast C-based tracing and outputs results
5. Reli handles output passthrough and process management

This approach gives users phpspy's performance benefits while gaining reli's ZTS support and address resolution capabilities.

## Documentation
Updated README with new "Hybrid phpspy mode" section documenting:
- Installation instructions
- Single-process tracing usage
- Daemon mode usage
- Available options and configuration

author: andreidanila1
body:
## Existent problem

Connecting to a device-heavy IIO context (e.g. M2k, ADRV9009) caused the IIOExplorer UI to freeze for several seconds before becoming responsive. Profiling identified two root causes:
                               
### Stylesheet propagation over hundreds of already-constructed widgets          
   
Style::setBackground is called in IIOExplorer::setupUI, after IIOModel has already been constructed with all its IIOWidget children attached to m_mainWidget. Setting a stylesheet on a parent widget triggers Qt to recursively re-polish every child widget in the hierarchy. With hundreds of IIOWidgets already attached, this single call accounted for 64.7% of the total freeze.
 
### Blocking IIOWidget construction on the UI thread                             
   
IIOModel::IIOModel built all IIOWidget instances for every device and channel attribute at connection time. Internally, IIOWidgetBuilder::createUIS() performs synchronous libiio reads for every attribute that exposes an _available variant:        

```
res = iio_channel_attr_read(m_channel, m_optionsAttribute, buffer, ATTR_BUFFER_SIZE);                                                              
res = iio_device_attr_read(m_device,  m_optionsAttribute, buffer, ATTR_BUFFER_SIZE); 
```                                                             
                  
These reads are blocking network calls (USB/IP backend) made on the UI thread, one per attribute, before the window even appears. On a device with 20 channels × 5 _available attributes this results in 100 sequential blocking reads. Beyond the libiio reads, IIOWidgets construction itself is expensive (especially for device-heavy contexts) - each widget goes through style application, layout setup (and others) at creation time.

## Changes

- Postpone IIOWidget construction to first expand/select
  - Building IIOWidgets for every device and channel attribute at connection time caused multi-second UI freezes on device-heavy contexts (e.g. M2k, ADRV9009).
- Background population of all device/channel nodes
  - Populate the IIOTree nodes in different QEvents to prevent the application from freezing. I also retain the previous commit's functionality, allowing a node to be loaded on demand by selecting or expanding it.
- IIOExplorer API updates

## Tested on

I've tested this on Ubuntu 22.10, Kuiper 2-64, and Windows ADI using the ADRV9009 multidevice emu. 
If possible, please also test on arm32 (and arm64) as well as macOS. 
On Ubuntu, the performance improved from 4 seconds to 100 ms, and on Kuiper from ~50 seconds to ~2 seconds.

**New Benchmark Functionality:**

* Added two new entrypoints, `ordered_range_query_duckdb` and `ordered_range_query_postgis`, that execute a spatial query with ordering and LIMIT for DuckDB and PostGIS, respectively. body:
## Trigger
Fatal Application log entries during startup RPC initialization (2 occurrences).

## Sample Logs
```
Startup RPC: 
Result: {}
```

## Root Cause
ApplicationImp::setup logs startup RPC commands/results at fatal severity and attempts to execute empty/invalid [rpc_startup] lines, producing empty command/result logs.

## Changes
- src/xrpld/app/main/Application.cpp: trim and skip empty startup RPC lines, log parse failures as errors, and log startup command/result at info.

## Before / After
- **Before**: Startup RPC entries (including empty ones) were logged at fatal level and invalid lines were still executed, yielding empty fatal logs.
- **After**: Empty startup RPC lines are ignored, parse failures are logged as errors without execution, and startup command/result logs use info severity.

## Risk
Low. Changes only affect logging severity and skip empty/invalid startup entries; valid startup RPC behavior remains unchanged.

author: jamestelfer
body:
## Purpose

Prepares the CI pipeline for dual deployment to both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages by producing two distinct artifacts from a single build.

The existing `withastro/action` is an all-in-one action that bundles setup, install, build, and artifact upload into a black box. It only uploads a GitHub Pages artifact, which is insufficient for the upcoming Cloudflare Pages deployment that needs a generic `dist/` artifact. Replacing it with explicit steps makes both artifacts available and gives the pipeline full control over the build process.

The workflow now also triggers on pull requests, enabling preview deployments in a future step. GitHub Pages deployment is guarded by an `if` condition so it only runs on push to main — PR builds run the full build and artifact upload without triggering a live deployment.

## Context

- Part of the Cloudflare Pages migration epic (chinmina-docs-7yn)
- Prerequisite for adding the Cloudflare Pages deployment job (chinmina-docs-7yn.2)
